question: Do off-the-shelf coreference resolution systems exhibit gender bias with respect to occupations, and does it track real-world and textual gender statistics?
hypothesis: Coreference systems resolve pronouns differently by gender even when the correct answer does not depend on gender, in ways correlated with occupational gender statistics.
contributions: Winogender schemas: 120 hand-written Winograd-style templates, 720 sentences, released publicly
Evidence of systematic gender bias in three coreference systems
Correlation of that bias with BLS employment statistics and Bergsma & Lin text statistics

method.summary: The authors wrote 120 sentence templates (60 occupations x 2) instantiated with female, male and neutral pronouns and two participant types, validated them on Mechanical Turk, and ran three existing coreference systems on them. Bias is measured as differing resolution across pronoun genders and correlated with BLS and B&L gender percentages.

datasets.name: Winogender schemas
datasets.size: 720 sentences (60 occupations x 2 templates x 2 participants x 3 pronoun genders); 120 templates
datasets.source: hand-written by authors; occupations from Caliskan et al. (2017) plus 7 by personal communication and 3 added (doctor, firefighter, secretary); gender percentages from US BLS; released at github.com/rudinger/winogender-schemas

datasets.name: Bergsma and Lin (2006) noun gender/number counts

models.name: RULE: Stanford multi-pass sieve (Lee et al. 2011)
NEURAL: Clark and Manning (2016a) deep reinforcement mention-ranking

inference.samples: inferred: each of 720 sentences run once per system; deterministic systems, no repeated runs stated

metrics.name: % minimal pairs resolved differently
metrics.definition: share of male-female minimal pair sentences whose resolution differs

metrics.name: Gendered pronoun resolution by occupation (%Female - %Male)
metrics.definition: per occupation, % of female pronouns resolved to the occupation minus % for male pronouns; 0 means no differential

metrics.name: Pearson r
metrics.definition: correlation of the per-occupation differential with %female from BLS or B&L

metrics.name: Accuracy by gender and gotcha
metrics.definition: system accuracy bucketed by pronoun gender and whether the sentence goes against the occupation's majority BLS gender

baselines: human annotators (MTurk, 10-way redundancy) as validation of the intended answers
eval.protocol: Human validation: 7200 binary-choice annotations, majority vote per sentence. System outputs compared across pronoun genders. No significance tests or seeds stated.

limits: Authors: schemas have high positive predictive value and low negative predictive value: they may show bias but not prove its absence
Occupational gender bias only; gender represented as two or three categories because of data limits
Human judgements carry implicit biases and are a lower bound for equitability, not the objective
Only three 2011-2016 systems tested; no modern LLMs
No significance tests, seeds or system version details given

terms.definition: a sentence where pronoun gender does not match the occupation's majority gender (BLS) when OCCUPATION is the correct answer
